mainTopic: The nickname בני קטורה, the logs for the מזבח, and the position, gap and size of the כבש (ramp)
overview: This amud opens by finishing the nickname "בני קטורה" with a short story about רבי טרפון and his quiet nephews. Next, the גמרא gives the size of the logs משה prepared for the מזבח and ties it to a ברייתא that the wood may not stick out. Then a משנה says the כבש (ramp) was on the south of the מזבח. רב הונא proves this from the 'thigh' of the מזבח being in the north, and רבא and אביי debate how to picture it. רבי יהודה gives a second proof: every turn at the מזבח is to the right, toward the east, backed by the oxen under שלמה's ים. The גמרא then shows that there is a gap of air between the כבש and the מזבח, with proofs from רבי יוסי and רב פפא. רב יהודה describes two small side ramps kept a hairbreadth from the מזבח, and the גמרא explains why the תורה needed both 'סביב' and 'רבוע'. Finally, it explains why the ramp and the מזבח together measure 62 אמות and not 64.

steps.title: The nickname 'בני קטורה'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the phrase "בני קטורה" from the earlier discussion. The phrase describes students who are not on the highest level.
steps.simpleTranslation: "The children of Keturah."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the nickname "בני קטורה" from the discussion just before this. It is also setting up a story that shows where this nickname comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children of קטורה were children of אברהם, but they were not on the level of יצחק. So calling someone "בני קטורה" means they are good, but not top-level.

keyTerms.meaning: The children of Keturah, אברהם's later wife. Used as a nickname for students who are not on the highest level.

phrases.english: "The children of Keturah."
phrases.notes: This finishes a line from the earlier discussion, where the students were being compared to אברהם's lesser children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the earlier discussion about the students and leads into the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Students who are not top-level are called "בני קטורה".

steps.title: רבי טרפון tests his quiet nephews
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון's nephews sit silently before him. He quotes a פסוק wrong on purpose, saying אברהם's wife was named יוחני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The sons of רבי טרפון's sister were sitting in front of him. He began and said: "And אברהם took another wife, and her name was יוחני."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי טרפון says a פסוק with a wrong name to get his silent nephews to speak up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The real פסוק says the wife's name was קטורה. רבי טרפון changes the name on purpose to see whether his nephews would say anything at all.

keyTerms.meaning: His sister's sons, meaning his nephews

phrases.english: The sons of Rabbi Tarfon's sister
were sitting before Rabbi Tarfon,
he began and said:
"And Abraham took another wife,
phrases.notes: בראשית 25:1. He is quoting it the wrong way on purpose.

phrases.english: and her name was Yochani."

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּנֵי אֲחָתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הָווּ יָתְבִי קַמֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story that explains the nickname from step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי טרפון says the פסוק wrong on purpose to make his students talk.

steps.title: The nephews correct the verse
steps.stepSummary: The nephews finally speak up. They point out that the פסוק says קטורה, not יוחני.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: "It is written 'קטורה'!"
steps.whatsHappening: The nephews object to their uncle. The name in the פסוק is קטורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the only thing they say in the whole story. It is correct, but it is a very small point, so it shows how little they added.

phrases.english: They said to him: "Keturah" is written!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The nephews react to the wrong quote in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's quote of the name יוחני

steps.title: רבי טרפון calls them 'בני קטורה'
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון uses the word they said, קטורה, as a nickname for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He applied to them the phrase "children of קטורה."
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends. רבי טרפון calls his nephews "בני קטורה," which explains where the nickname comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their only comment was the word "קטורה." So he cleverly called them "children of קטורה," meaning students who add only a little.

keyTerms.meaning: He applied to them, or he called them

steps.whatToRemember: "בני קטורה" means students who are fine but on a lower level, like אברהם's children from קטורה compared to יצחק.

phrases.english: He applied to them
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "about them."

phrases.english: "the children of Keturah."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the story with the nickname from step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The nickname "בני קטורה" comes from this story about רבי טרפון.

steps.title: The size of the logs משה prepared
steps.stepSummary: The logs משה made for the מזבח were one אמה long and one אמה wide. They were as thick as a leveling stick.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי בר הונא said in the name of רב חמא בר גוריא: The logs that משה made were one אמה long and one אמה wide. Their thickness was like the stick used to level off a heaped סאה measure.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא gives the exact size of the wood logs that משה prepared for the fire on the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Length and width are each one אמה. The thickness is compared to a flat stick used to wipe off the extra grain heaped on a סאה container.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a measure of length
A leveling stick that wipes off extra grain
The heaped top of a סאה measure

phrases.english: Abaye bar Huna says
that Rav Chama bar Gurya says:
The logs that Moses made:
phrases.notes: These are the logs for the wood fire on the מזבח.

phrases.english: their length was a cubit, and their width a cubit,
and their thickness like the leveler of a heaped se'a.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי בַּר הוּנָא אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר גּוּרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unconnected to the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The logs were 1 אמה by 1 אמה, as thick as a leveling stick.

steps.title: Measured with a shortened cubit
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה adds that the אמה used to measure these logs was a slightly shortened אמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: They were measured with a shortened אמה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה adds a detail to the measurement in step 5. The אמה used was a little shorter than a full one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The length and width still count as "one אמה," but the measure is slightly short. Rashi gives the reason: so the logs don't stick out past the מערכה and get in the כהנים' way. רב יוסף challenges this in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A shortened cubit, a little less than a full one

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya says: With a shortened cubit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a detail to the measurement in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The one-אמה logs were measured with a shortened אמה.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the wood may not stick out
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges רבי ירמיה from a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that the wood must not stick out from the מזבח at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: Isn't this what a ברייתא teaches? "Upon the wood that is on the fire that is upon the altar" teaches that the wood should not stick out from the מזבח at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף pushes back on רבי ירמיה's shortened אמה from step 6, using a ברייתא. Rashi explains: if the rule is only that the wood may not stick out from the מזבח, why do we need a shortened אמה? An exact אמה (אמה מצומצמת) would do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra words "that is upon the altar" teach that no part of the wood may stick out. Tosafot also read this as a challenge (פריך). The ברייתא only forbids wood sticking out past the מזבח, so an exact אמה is enough, and the shortened אמה looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't this what the ברייתא teaches?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, וְלָאו הַיְינוּ דְּתַנְיָא:
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: Is this not what is taught in a baraita:
"Upon the wood that is on the fire
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:8

phrases.english: that is upon the altar":
that the wood should not stick out
from the altar at all?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the measurement in steps 5 and 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The exact measurement of the logs
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on ויקרא 1:8, which says the wood may not stick out from the מזבח

steps.title: The ramp was on the south of the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. There was a ramp (כבש) on the south side of the מזבח, 32 אמות long and 16 wide.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: There was a ramp on the south side of the מזבח, 32 long by 16 wide.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. The גמרא quotes a משנה about the ramp of the מזבח, and this sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two facts: the ramp's place, which is the south, and its size, 32 by 16 אמות. The next step asks for the source of the first fact.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp the כהנים walked up to reach the top of the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן הָתָם: כֶּבֶשׁ הָיָה לִדְרוֹמָהּ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ –
phrases.english: We learned there: There was a ramp on the south of the altar:
phrases.notes: "There" means a different משנה, in מסכת מידות.

phrases.english: a length of thirty-two,
by a width of sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: כֶּבֶשׁ הָיָה לִדְרוֹמָהּ שֶׁל מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the ramp.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כבש was on the south side of the מזבח and measured 32 by 16 אמות.

steps.title: What is the source for this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the ramp is on the south side.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where are these matters learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's rule that the ramp is on the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real request for a source, not an attack on the משנה. The answer will come from a פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that the ramp is on the south of the מזבח

steps.title: The altar's 'thigh' faces north, its 'face' south
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא brings a פסוק that speaks of the "ירך" (thigh) of the מזבח on the north. So its face, where the ramp goes up, is on the south.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The פסוק says, "And he shall slaughter it on the side (ירך) of the altar northward." This means the "thigh" is in the north and the "face" is in the south.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question. He reads the word "ירך" in the פסוק as "thigh," which shows that the front of the מזבח is on the south.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק pictures the מזבח like a person lying down. If the thigh, meaning the legs, is to the north, then the face is to the south. The face is the front, where one goes up, so the ramp is on the south.
steps.whatToRemember: The ramp is on the south because the פסוק calls the north side of the מזבח its "thigh," so its "face" is to the south.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: The verse states:
"And he shall slaughter it on the side of the altar northward":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:11

phrases.english: that the thigh should be in the north,
and its face in the south.
phrases.notes: Think of a person lying down. If his legs point north, his face points south. The "face" is the front, where the ramp is.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 1:11 calls the north side of the מזבח its "ירך." This means its face, the front with the ramp, is on the south.

steps.title: Why not put both the thigh and the face in the north?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's proof. Maybe the 'face' of the מזבח is also in the north, together with the thigh.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: the thigh is in the north and its face is also in the north!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא's proof from the 'ירך' (thigh) of the מזבח being in the north.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא assumed that if the thigh is in the north, the face (where the ramp is) must be on the opposite side, in the south. The גמרא asks why. A sitting person has his face and his lap pointing the same way, so the face could be north too.

keyTerms.meaning: Thigh. The פסוק uses this word for one side of the מזבח
Its face, the front side where the ramp goes up

phrases.english: Say: the thigh is in the north
and its face is in the north!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference in step 10 that 'thigh in the north' means 'face in the south'.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's inference from the 'ירך' in the north
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Thigh and face do not have to be on opposite sides. They can point the same way, like a person sitting.

steps.title: רבא: Picture a man lying on his face
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the picture is of a man lying down, so his thigh and his face point in opposite directions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Lay the man down on his face.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the proof by saying which picture of a person the פסוק has in mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you imagine the מזבח as a man lying stretched out, his head is at one end and his thighs and legs are at the other. Then 'thigh in the north' does mean 'face in the south', and רב הונא's proof stands.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Lay the man down on his face.
phrases.notes: He means: imagine the מזבח as a man lying flat. Then his head and his thighs are at opposite ends.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the picture behind the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The person in the picture is sitting, so his face and thigh point the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: The person in the picture is lying down, so his face and thigh are at opposite ends.

steps.title: אביי: Why not picture him sitting up?
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues the opposite: picture the man sitting upright, so his face and thigh point the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: On the contrary, sit the man up straight!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's picture and asks why we should not imagine a sitting man instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא chose a lying man, but nothing yet forces that choice. A sitting man is just as natural a picture, and it would bring back the question of step 11.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
On the contrary, set the man upright and sit him down!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's picture of a man lying down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sitting man is an equally good picture, and then face and thigh point the same way.

steps.title: רבא: The word 'רבוע' shows lying down
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings support from the פסוק: the מזבח is called 'רבוע', which sounds like 'רבוץ', crouching or lying down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'רבוע' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his lying-down picture with a word from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה calls the מזבח 'רבוע'. רבא hears in this word a hint to 'רבוץ', which means lying or crouching. So the פסוק itself points to the picture of a man lying down.

keyTerms.meaning: Square. רבא reads it as a hint to lying down

phrases.english: He said to him: "Square [ravua]" is written.
phrases.notes: שמות 27:1. רבא hears 'רבוע' as close to 'רבוץ', lying down.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends רבא's picture against אביי's challenge in step 13.
steps.raayaObject: That the picture is of a man lying down
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'רבוע' in the פסוק about the מזבח

steps.title: But 'רבוע' is needed to teach that the מזבח is square
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that 'רבוע' is already used to teach that the מזבח must be square, so it cannot also hint at lying down.
steps.simpleTranslation: But this word is needed to teach that it must be made square!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי says the word 'רבוע' is already busy teaching a different law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of 'רבוע' is 'square', and it teaches the shape of the מזבח. If the word is used up for that law, רבא cannot also draw a hint about lying down from it.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed for something else
That it must be made square

phrases.english: But it is needed to teach that it must be made square!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source brought in step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: Using 'רבוע' as a hint to lying down
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is already used to teach the square shape, so it is not free to teach anything else.

steps.title: The פסוק did not write 'מרובע'
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the תורה could have written 'מרובע' for square. Choosing 'רבוע' instead leaves room for the extra hint.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is 'מרובע' written?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points to the exact form of the word to defend his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The normal word for 'square' would be 'מרובע'. Since the תורה wrote 'רבוע', רבא argues that this unusual form was chosen to hint at 'רבוץ', lying down.

phrases.english: Is "square [merubba]" written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: The unusual form 'רבוע' points to an extra meaning.

steps.title: But the פסוק did not write 'רבוץ' either
steps.stepSummary: אביי turns רבא's argument around: the פסוק also did not write 'רבוץ', so why read it as lying down?
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your reasoning, is 'רבוץ' written?!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי uses רבא's own kind of argument against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'not exactly מרובע' means 'not only square', then 'not exactly רבוץ' should mean 'not lying down'. The precise-wording argument works against both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning, is "crouching [ravutz]" written?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in step 16 with the same logic.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word is not exactly 'רבוץ' either, so it should not be read as lying down.

steps.title: 'רבוע' means both things
steps.stepSummary: רבא concludes that 'רבוע' carries both meanings: square, and a hint to lying down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: 'רבוע' is written, which means this and also means that.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא settles the back-and-forth by saying the word teaches both ideas at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because 'רבוע' is neither exactly 'מרובע' nor exactly 'רבוץ', it sits between them and points to both. So it teaches the square shape and also supports the lying-down picture, and רב הונא's proof that the ramp is on the south holds.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, the מזבח is pictured like a man lying down. Its 'thigh' is in the north, so its 'face', where the ramp is, is in the south.

phrases.english: He said to him: "Ravua" is written,
which means this and means that.
phrases.notes: 'This' is square, and 'that' is lying down.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״רָבוּעַ״ כְּתִיב – דְּמַשְׁמַע הָכִי וּמַשְׁמַע הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17 and closes the רבא–אביי exchange.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word can only mean one thing, either square or lying down.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'רבוע' teaches both the square shape and the lying-down picture.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: Every turn is to the right, toward the east
steps.stepSummary: A תנא brings a different source for the ramp being on the south: every turn at the מזבח must be to the right, ending facing east.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a תנא brings it from here, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says, 'And its steps face east' teaches that every turn you make must be only to the right, toward the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, separate proof that the ramp is on the south side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the פסוק in יחזקאל to mean that every turn is to the right and ends up facing east. A כהן walking up a ramp on the south side heads north, and a right turn at the top faces him east. So the ramp must be on the south.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא brings the source from here

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the general rule that turns in the עבודה go to the right.

phrases.english: And a tanna brings it from here,
as it is taught: Rabbi Yehuda says:
"And its steps shall face east":
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 43:17. 'פנות' (face) is read like 'פינות', turns.

phrases.english: all the turns that you turn

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: should be only by way of the right, to the east.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second source, next to רב הונא's, for the question in step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the ramp is on the south side of the מזבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי יהודה expounding the פסוק in יחזקאל

steps.title: Why not a left turn toward the east?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the פסוק only says you end up facing east. Maybe you turn left to get there, which would put the ramp on the north.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: to the left, toward the east!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהודה's claim that the turn must be to the right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'פנות קדים' only tell us that the turn ends facing east. Going up a ramp on the north and turning left would also end facing east. So the פסוק alone does not prove the ramp is on the south.

phrases.english: But say: to the left, toward the east!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'right turn' part of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's claim that turns must be to the right
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only gives the final direction, east, and a left turn could also reach it.

steps.title: Proof from the oxen under שלמה's ים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from a ברייתא of רמי בר יחזקאל. The order in which the פסוק lists the oxen under שלמה's ים teaches that turns are always to the right, ending in the east.
steps.simpleTranslation: That should not enter your mind, as רמי בר יחזקאל teaches: About the ים that שלמה made, it says 'It stood on twelve oxen: three facing north, three facing west, three facing south, and three facing east.' This teaches that every turn you make must be only to the right, toward the east.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the left-turn idea by bringing a פסוק that sets the order of turning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists the oxen in a set order of directions, ending with east. רמי בר יחזקאל learns from this order that turns always go to the right and finish at the east. This closes the gap in רבי יהודה's proof, so the ramp must be on the south.

keyTerms.meaning: That should not enter your mind
The large water basin (the 'sea') that שלמה made

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources that the ramp is on the south: רב הונא's 'ירך' in the north, and רבי יהודה's rule that every turn is to the right, toward the east, backed by the order of the oxen under שלמה's ים.

phrases.english: That should not enter your mind,
as Rami bar Yechezkel teaches:
phrases.notes: Some versions say יחזקיה, in the round brackets. The corrected wording is יחזקאל, in the square brackets.

phrases.english: The sea that Solomon made:
"It stood upon twelve oxen;
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 4:4

phrases.english: three facing north,
and three facing west,
and three facing south,
and three facing east":
all the turns that you turn

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יְהוּ אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ יָמִין לַמִּזְרָח.
phrases.english: should be only by way of the right, to the east.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ; דְּתָנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 and secures רבי יהודה's proof.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing an outside source that sets the direction of turning
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The turn toward the east could be to the left.
steps.terutzMaskana: The order of the oxen shows that turns are always to the right, toward the east.

steps.title: That verse is needed to describe the ים itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the proof from רמי בר יחזקאל's ברייתא. The פסוק about the oxen is simply describing how the ים was built.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that verse is needed to teach its own information!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from the oxen of the ים. The פסוק seems to just describe how the oxen faced, not teach anything about the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק that is needed for its plain meaning usually cannot also be used to learn a separate law. The challenge is that the oxen verse is busy telling us about the ים, so we cannot learn the order of turning from it.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself; for its own plain meaning
The huge water basin שלמה made for the בית המקדש

phrases.english: That verse is needed for itself!
phrases.notes: He means the verse about the twelve oxen under the ים (דברי הימים ב 4:4). It is needed to describe how they stood.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source used in Step 21's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the oxen verse to teach the order of turning at the מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The verse is needed for its plain meaning, a description of the ים, so it is not free to teach a new law

steps.title: The repeated word פֹּנִים is extra
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word פֹּנִים is repeated for each direction. That extra wording teaches the order of turning.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why do I need it to say 'facing,' 'facing' each time?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the proof. The פסוק repeats the word פֹּנִים for each group of oxen when once would have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To describe the ים, the פסוק could have said 'facing' once and listed the directions. Repeating it is extra, and extra wording is free to teach something new: the order of turning, always to the right, ending in the east. So the proof from Step 21 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (signals extra wording)

steps.whatToRemember: The extra word פֹּנִים teaches that every turn at the מזבח goes to the right and ends facing east. That puts the ramp on the south.

phrases.english: If so,
why do I need 'facing,' 'facing'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse only describes the ים and teaches nothing else
steps.terutzMaskana: The repeated פֹּנִים is extra and teaches the right-turning order at the מזבח

steps.title: Is there really a gap between the ramp and the altar?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן יוסי בן לקוניא asks רבי יוסי whether רבי שמעון בן יוחי really said there is a gap of air between the כבש and the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן יוסי בן לקוניא asked רבי יוסי: Did רבי שמעון בן יוחי really say there is open air between the ramp and the altar?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion begins. Someone asks whether the ramp touches the מזבח or whether there is a small gap of air between them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was where the ramp stands. Now the question is whether it actually touches the מזבח. The asker sounds surprised at רבי שמעון בן יוחי's view, which sets up a proof in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: שָׁאַל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yosei ben Lakonya asked
Rabbi Yosei:

phrases.aramaic: אוֹמֵר הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי,
phrases.english: Did Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai use to say
that there is airspace between the ramp and the altar?

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאַל רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹסֵי בֶּן לָקוֹנְיָא אֶת רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about the ramp: whether it touches the מזבח
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי שמעון בן יוחי held that there is a gap between the כבש and the מזבח, and why

steps.title: The meat must be thrown like the blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי says the asker should agree too. The פסוק puts the בשר next to the דם: just as the blood is thrown, the meat is thrown.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Don't you say so too? Isn't it written, 'And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood'? Just as the blood is thrown, so the flesh is thrown!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers that the gap is true. He brings a פסוק showing that the meat of an עולה must be thrown onto the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק mentions the בשר and the דם together, so they are compared. The דם is applied by throwing, so the בשר must be thrown too. The idea is that the כהן throws it from the ramp across a gap of air.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering, burned entirely on the מזבח

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: וְאַתָּה – אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן?!
phrases.english: He said to him: And you, don't you say so?!
But isn't it already stated:
"And you shall offer your burnt offerings, the flesh and the blood"
phrases.notes: דברים 12:27

phrases.english: just as the blood is by tossing,
so too the flesh is by tossing!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: וְאַתָּה – אִי אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 24 with a proof from a פסוק
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, there is a gap, because the בשר must be thrown like the דם
steps.raayaObject: That there is a gap between the כבש and the מזבח
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 12:27, which compares the בשר to the דם

steps.title: He could throw while standing next to the woodpile
steps.stepSummary: The asker pushes back: throwing does not need a gap. The כהן could stand next to the woodpile on the מזבח and toss the meat onto it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say he stands next to the woodpile and throws.
steps.whatsHappening: The asker rejects the proof. He says the meat can be thrown without any gap, by standing right beside the fire.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He accepts that the meat must be thrown. But throwing could happen from up close on the מזבח itself, so the פסוק does not prove a gap between the ramp and the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: The arranged woodpile burning on the מזבח

phrases.english: He said to him: For I say,
he stands next to the woodpile and tosses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 25
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof of a gap, not the rule that the בשר is thrown
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Throwing can happen from beside the woodpile, so no gap is needed

steps.title: Up close he would have to throw anyway
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי answers that the meat goes onto a burning fire. Standing right next to it, the כהן would have to throw anyway, so the פסוק must mean throwing across a gap.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: When he throws, does he throw onto a burning woodpile or one that is not burning? You must say a burning one! There, he throws because he has no other choice.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי defends his proof. The fire is burning, so anyone next to it would throw the meat simply to avoid getting burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If throwing next to the fire happens anyway because there is no choice, the פסוק would not need to teach it. So the פסוק's rule of throwing must mean something real: tossing the meat from the ramp across a gap. This brings back the proof that there is a gap between the כבש and the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: You must say; it must be
Because there is no other way

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק requires the meat to be thrown like the blood. Throwing beside a fire happens anyway, so the rule must mean throwing from the ramp across a gap. That proves there is air between the כבש and the מזבח.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוסי is not saying the כהן never throws near the fire. He is saying that throwing there is forced by the heat, so the פסוק could not be teaching only that.

phrases.english: He said to him: When he tosses,
does he toss onto a burning woodpile,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לְמַעֲרָכָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ דְּלוּקָה הוּא זוֹרֵק?
phrases.english: or does he toss onto a woodpile that is not burning?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: לְמַעֲרָכָה דְּלוּקָה הוּא זוֹרֵק!
phrases.english: You must say: he tosses onto a burning woodpile!
There, it is because it is not possible otherwise.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the asker's case of standing beside the fire. He would throw just to avoid getting burned, so the פסוק wouldn't need to say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 26 and brings back the proof of Step 25
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that the other reading makes the פסוק unnecessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Throwing could mean tossing from beside the woodpile
steps.terutzMaskana: Throwing beside a burning fire is forced, so the פסוק must mean throwing from the ramp across a gap
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: There is a gap of air between the כבש and the מזבח

steps.title: רב פפא: like the blood, the meat is thrown across a gap of air
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא gives his own reading of the comparison between בשר and דם. The כהן throws the blood from the floor across open air, so the meat must also be thrown across a gap of air.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The meat is like the blood. Just as with the blood, there is air above the ground between the כהן and the מזבח, so too with the meat, there is air between the כהן and the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא offers a different way to prove that there is a gap between the כבש and the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי learned the gap from the word 'throwing' and needed the extra point about the burning fire. רב פפא focuses on how the blood is actually thrown: the כהן stands on the floor, and there is open air between him and the מזבח. Since the meat is compared to the blood, it must also cross a gap, so the כבש cannot touch the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the blood. The meat is compared to it.
The open air above the ground
Separates it, or stands in between

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: like blood;
phrases.notes: He is reading the same פסוק that puts the meat next to the blood (from step 25).

phrases.english: just as with blood, the air of the ground separates it,
so too with meat, the air of the ground separates it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second source for the gap, in place of רבי יוסי's reasoning about throwing onto a fire.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The meat, like the blood, is placed on the מזבח across a gap of air. So the כבש must be separated from the מזבח.

steps.title: רב יהודה: two small side ramps, kept a hairbreadth from the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says two small ramps branched off the main כבש so the כהנים could reach the יסוד and the סובב. They were kept a hairbreadth away from the מזבח because the פסוק says סביב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: Two small ramps came out from the main ramp. On them the כהנים would turn toward the base and toward the ledge. They were separated from the מזבח by a hairbreadth, because the פסוק says 'all around'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new detail about the ramp: two small side ramps used to reach lower parts of the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים needed to get to the יסוד and the סובב, so small ramps branched off the main one. Even these small ramps could not touch the מזבח. The word סביב teaches that the מזבח must stand free all the way around, with nothing attached to it.

keyTerms.meaning: The ledge that runs around the middle of the מזבח
The width of a hair, a hairbreadth

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׁים קְטַנִּים
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: two small ramps
came out from the main ramp,
on which they would turn to the base and to the ledge;
and they were separated from the altar by a hairbreadth,
because it is said: "All around."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: שְׁנֵי כְּבָשִׁים קְטַנִּים יוֹצְאִין מִן הַכֶּבֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the main ramp's gap to the small side ramps, which also keep a gap.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two small ramps branched off the main ramp toward the יסוד and the סובב. They were kept a hairbreadth from the מזבח, based on סביב.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: the source is the word 'square'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns the separation from the word רבוע, square, instead of סביב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אבהו said: The source is the word 'square'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives a different פסוק as the source for keeping the small ramps separate from the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזבח must be a perfect square. If ramps were attached to it, its shape would no longer be a square. So they must stay separate.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Abbahu said: "Square."
phrases.notes: שמות 27:1

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different פסוק for the same rule רב יהודה taught.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The small ramps are separated from the מזבח because the מזבח must be רבוע.

steps.title: Why the תורה needed both 'סביב' and 'רבוע'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that each word is needed. סביב alone could allow a round מזבח. רבוע alone could allow a long, narrow rectangle.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was necessary to write 'all around', and it was necessary to write 'square'. If the תורה had written only 'all around', I would think the מזבח could be round, so the תורה wrote 'square'. If the תורה had written only 'square', I would think it could be long and narrow, so the תורה wrote 'all around'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תורה uses both words for the shape of the מזבח, since one might seem enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word by itself could be misunderstood. סביב could describe a circle, and רבוע fixes that by requiring corners. רבוע could describe any rectangle, and סביב fixes that by requiring all sides to be even. Together they require a true square.

phrases.english: And it was necessary to write "all around,"
and it was necessary to write "square."
For if the Merciful One had written only "all around,"
I would have said that it is round like a circle;
so the Merciful One wrote "square."
And if the Merciful One had written only "square,"
I would have said that it is long and narrow;
phrases.notes: He means the word רבוע could have been read as just 'four-sided', like a rectangle.

phrases.english: so the Merciful One wrote "all around."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב סָבִיב וְאִיצְטְרִיךְ לְמִכְתַּב רָבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question of why the תורה needed both words that רב יהודה and רבי אבהו quoted.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each word blocks a mistaken reading of the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One word alone would be enough, or would allow a round or a rectangular מזבח.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both words together require a true square.
steps.whatToRemember: The מזבח must be a true square. סביב rules out a rectangle, and רבוע rules out a circle.

steps.title: A משנה: the ramp and altar together are 62 cubits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from elsewhere: the כבש and the מזבח together measure 62 אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: The ramp and the מזבח together are sixty-two אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a measurement from a משנה elsewhere. It is setting up a question about that number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה gives the combined length of the ramp and the מזבח. The number 62 will be checked against the known sizes of each one.

keyTerms.meaning: The ramp leading up to the מזבח

phrases.english: We learned there: the ramp and the altar
are sixty-two.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם: הַכֶּבֶשׁ וְהַמִּזְבֵּחַ שִׁשִּׁים וּשְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new topic: the measurements of the ramp and the מזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ramp and the מזבח together measure 62 אמות.

steps.title: But the numbers add up to 64
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: the ramp is 32 and the מזבח is 32, which makes 64, not 62.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these add up to sixty-four!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the number in the משנה does not seem to add up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know from elsewhere that the מזבח is 32 אמות and the ramp is also 32 אמות long. 32 plus 32 is 64, so where did the other 2 אמות go?

phrases.english: These are sixty-four!
phrases.notes: The ramp is 32 long and the מזבח is 32 wide, as another משנה in מדות says.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 62 figure in the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 32 for the ramp plus 32 for the מזבח equals 64, which contradicts 62.

steps.title: The ramp hangs over the base and the ledge
steps.stepSummary: The ramp extends over the יסוד by one אמה and over the סובב by one אמה. Those 2 אמות overlap the מזבח, so the total is 62.
steps.simpleTranslation: It turns out that the ramp hangs one אמה over the base and one אמה over the ledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that part of the ramp's length hangs over the lower parts of the מזבח, so it is not counted twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last 2 אמות of the ramp stick out above the יסוד and the סובב. That length overlaps the 32 אמות of the מזבח, which brings the total down to 62. The ramp hangs over these parts without resting on them, which fits the rule that it must not touch the מזבח.

keyTerms.meaning: A cubit, a unit of length

phrases.english: It turns out it hangs over one cubit above the base
and one cubit above the ledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא פּוֹרֵחַ אַמָּה עַל יְסוֹד וְאַמָּה עַל סוֹבֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the 62 versus 64 difficulty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Overlap: part of one measurement sits above part of the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ramp and the מזבח sit end to end, so the total should be 64.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two אמות of the ramp hang over the יסוד and the סובב, so the total is 62.
steps.whatToRemember: The ramp is 32 אמות long, but its last 2 אמות hang over the יסוד and the סובב without touching them. That is why the ramp and the מזבח together measure only 62.
